objectives: Consolidate the taught m/s/t/a/p sound-symbol relationships.
Check decoding, phoneme discrimination, spelling and connected-text comprehension separately.
Identify specific needs for targeted remediation before new phonics content.
concepts: A phonics checkpoint should separate component skills.
Accurate decoding requires blending all taught phonemes.
Comprehension depends on reading the words and retaining meaning.

definitions.definition: An assessment used to identify strengths and specific learning needs for the next teaching step.
Using known letter-sound relationships to read a word.
Using sounds to construct the written spelling of a word.

workedExamples: If a learner misses the final sound in tap, practise final phoneme identification before advancing.
commonMistakes: Answering comprehension questions without returning to the text.
revisionPoints: m/s/t/a/p → identify → blend → decode → spell → comprehend.

conceptual: Match sound sequences to CVC words.
application: Decode and spell taught CVC words.
higherOrderThinking: Choose an appropriate response when decoding breaks down.
mixedReview: Combine phoneme identification, decoding, spelling and comprehension.

mistakeBasedRevision: Missing initial sound → practise onset identification.
Missing final sound → practise final phoneme.
weakTopicRevision: Use the missed skill category for targeted practice rather than repeating the whole lesson.

activities.name: Meaning check
steps: Return to the sentence to verify.

outcomes: Learner identifies taught m/s/t/a/p sound relationships with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner decodes taught CVC words with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner spells taught CVC words with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner answers controlled-text comprehension questions with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner's errors can be assigned to a specific remediation category.

questions.question: Which word has /s/ at the beginning?
Which word has /t/ at the beginning?
Read: “Pat sat.” What did Pat do?
Read: “Pat sat at a mat.” Where did Pat sit?
Which learner response shows accurate decoding?
options: Blending all taught sounds into the word

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot read a CVC word?
options: Say each taught sound and blend again

questions.question: Which area does a sentence question measure?
Which pattern is correct for the word “map”?
What is the purpose of this checkpoint?
options: Find strengths and needs before targeted practice
